record.paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
record.original_question: What is the mass composition of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays at the highest energies, especially around and above 10^20 eV, and does the observed trend toward heavier primaries near ultrahigh energies continue, flatten, or change when larger statistics and better hadronic-interaction modeling become available?

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, many aspects of the nature of UHECRs remain an enigma: What is the origin of these particles? What is their mass composition? How do the astrophysical sources accelerate particles to such extreme energies?
As of today, no composition fractions are available around and above 1020 eV.

These measurements of the ﬁrst two moments (mean and standard deviation) of theXmax distribution suggest that the composition of cosmic rays becomes lighter as the energy increases towards the ankle (until around 1018.3 eV) and then becomes heavier again when approaching ultrahigh energies.
Due to the limited statistics and unknowns about hadronic interaction models, this trend is still largely uncertain.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) are charged particles (atomic nuclei) of astrophysical origin observed with energies exceeding roughly 10^18 eV. Their primary mass is inferred indirectly from extensive air showers, principally via the depth of shower maximum X_max, whose first two moments (mean and standard deviation) are interpreted through hadronic-interaction Monte Carlo models to estimate the fractional abundances of light, intermediate, and heavy nuclear species as functions of primary energy E.

Existing measurements indicate that the mean primary mass decreases with E up to about 10^18.3 eV (the "ankle" of the energy spectrum) and then increases (composition becomes heavier) as E approaches 10^20 eV; however, no composition fractions have been established at and above E ≈ 10^20 eV due to limited event statistics and uncertainties in hadronic-interaction models.

Problem. With substantially increased exposure and improved hadronic-interaction modeling:

(a) Determine the mass composition (the fractional abundances of proton, helium, nitrogen/CNO, and iron-like primary nuclei) of UHECRs at energies E ≥ 10^20 eV.

(b) Decide whether the observed trend of increasing mean primary mass with energy in the range 10^18.3 eV ≲ E ≲ 10^20 eV continues monotonically toward heavier primaries above 10^20 eV, flattens to an approximately constant heavy composition, or changes character (for example, by re-emergence of a light component) at the highest energies.

Provide quantitative composition fractions with uncertainties at E ≥ 10^20 eV and a determination of the qualitative behavior in (b).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by the Pierre Auger Collaboration (2024) using deep-learning reconstruction has extended X_max-based composition measurements up to ~10^20 eV (100 EeV), indicating that the composition becomes increasingly heavier and purer with energy and is incompatible with a large light-nuclei fraction in the 50–100 EeV range, with three break features near spectral features. However, robust composition fractions strictly above 10^20 eV remain limited by statistics and hadronic-interaction-model uncertainties, so the question is best characterized as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Inference of the Mass Composition of Cosmic Rays with Energies from 10^18.5 to 10^20 eV Using the Pierre Auger Observatory and Deep Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Deep-learning-based inference of UHECR mass composition extending to 10^20 eV using Auger data.
status_evidence.claim: Composition has now been inferred up to ~10^20 eV, showing increasing mean mass and decreasing spread with energy.

status_evidence.title: AI-powered algorithm sheds new light on the mass composition of cosmic rays at ultra-high energies
status_evidence.snippet: The energy evolution of <X_max> and sigma(X_max) indicates the composition becomes increasingly heavier and purer, incompatible with a large fraction of light nuclei between 50 and 100 EeV.
status_evidence.claim: Composition trend toward heavier and purer primaries continues up to ~10^20 eV per Auger 2024 analysis.

status_evidence.title: Isotropy of cosmic rays beyond 10^20 eV favors their heavy mass composition
status_evidence.snippet: Arrival-direction isotropy above 10^20 eV is argued to favor a heavy primary composition.
status_evidence.claim: Independent anisotropy-based arguments support a heavy composition at the highest energies.
